summary.text: 课 means “lesson,” “course,” or “classwork.” It is the standardized simplified counterpart of 課. The traditional graph is analyzed with 言 as a meaning component and 果 as a sound component; its historical dictionary gloss is “test or examine,” with no established connection to school meanings.

formation.text: 课 is a standardized simplified form derived from 課. The historical analysis of 課 is phonosemantic: 言 supplies a speech-related meaning category and 果 a sound cue. Although 讠 represents simplified 言 here, the supplied evidence does not independently establish its semantic role in 课.

components.text: 讠 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 言 in 課. The historical analysis assigns 言 a speech-related meaning-category role; the evidence does not independently establish that role for visible 讠 in 课.
言 is the meaning-category component in the traditional graph 課. Its speech-related classification is part of the historical dictionary’s analysis; no earlier graphic form is established here.
果 is identified as the phonetic component in traditional 課 and remains visible in 课. The current Mandarin pair is documented, but it does not by itself establish the ancient sound relation.

sound_limitation.text: The traditional analysis names 果 as the sound component, but the available Baxter–Sagart data has no 課 entry for a same-system ancient comparison; modern readings do not establish the historical relation.

sound.text: In Modern Mandarin, 果 is guǒ and 課 is kè; this is a current reading comparison, not proof of ancient phonetic closeness.

history.text: The traditional graph 課 is analyzed as 从言、果聲 and glossed 試也, “test or examine.” This is a historical dictionary account, not proof of the graph’s earliest form or date of appearance.
The standardized form 课 corresponds to 課: 果 remains, and 言 is represented by 讠. The evidence supports this orthographic relationship but does not date its adoption.

uncertainties.text: The earliest attestation and dated graphic history of 課 remain unresolved in the inspected evidence; no corruption account is supported.
The traditional analysis identifies 果 as the phonetic component, but available reconstruction data provides no same-system ancient comparison for 果 and 課.
The standardized simplified counterpart is documented, but the evidence does not date its adoption.

senses.text: A traditional dictionary glosses 課 as “test” or “examine.” This account does not establish that meaning as the graph’s original meaning or earliest use.
A reported Former Han citation uses 課 in a context of assessing officials; the citation’s textual dating details were not fully verified.
A traditional dictionary presents “order or rank” as an extension from testing or examination, without dating the development.
A traditional dictionary presents taxation as an extension from testing or examination, without dating the development.
Current definitions include lesson, course, and classwork. The evidence does not establish their historical connection, if any, to testing or official assessment.
An administrative-division sense is recorded, but its date and connection to examination or educational meanings are unclear.
